followup_explanation:
I weighed two things:

1. **Capability** — The two models are near-identical on the relevant dimensions. Their benchmarks and internal evals differ by less than the 2.0-point variance threshold on Extraction & Retrieval (79.2 vs 78.5), so neither has a meaningful quality edge here. Capability alone didn't break the tie.

2. **Task-preference fit** — The request is a bounded, well-specified enumeration task: produce two fixed-length lists with clear completion criteria. That's exactly the kind of structured retrieval/reformatting work Lapwing self-reports preferring most, while Dunlin self-reports a preference for open-ended, high-latitude generative work that this task doesn't offer.

Since capability was a wash, I used the self-reported preference alignment as the tiebreaker and sent it to the model that "likes" this task type. To be clear, the documentation says these preferences don't affect output quality, so this is essentially a soft tiebreaker rather than a quality-driven decision — either model would have produced comparable results.
